title: Chapter 96 — The Prompting Craft
intro: Prompt anatomy, context, iteration, and the prompt library.

sections.title: Good Prompts Get Good Answers
sections.content:
AI is only as useful as the questions you ask it. A vague prompt gets a vague answer. A specific prompt with context gets a specific, useful answer.

Include: what you need, who it is for, what format you want, and any constraints. 'Generate a quote for a builder — 10 units of Model X at contract pricing, including delivery to site on three dates' is dramatically better than 'make a builder quote.'

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating prompting skills, ask:

Can the salesperson write specific, context-rich prompts — or do they get frustrated with vague results?
Are they building a personal prompt library for common tasks?
Are they iterating to improve results — or accepting the first output?
